manifest.name: dsh-plugin-hindsight-advanced
manifest.description: Long-term memory for DeepSeek Harness agents: automatic recall each turn, a retain/recall/reflect tool, standing rules, and visibility you scope to the whole bank, a preset, or a session.

bundle.text:
# dsh-plugin-hindsight-advanced bundle patch: the profile layer that mounts this
# package. `dsh plugin add` joins it into `dsh.profile.bundles` (the CLI
# reconciles the layer list against installed state).
#
# The row ships DISABLED — the install is inert. Two opt-in scopes (README):
# - per preset: a row in the preset's own agent.cordis.yml
#   (`name: dsh-plugin-hindsight-advanced`, its own `config` — that preset's bank).
#   Presets without the row are mount-less: no tool, no auto-recall.
# - for every preset: the user's profile patch layer
#   (~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml) enables this row:
#     - id: hindsight
#       disabled: false
#   An id-targeted `config` in that layer replaces the row's config block
#   whole (no deep merge).
#
# Never combine both: the host row and a preset row are two mounts, and the
# per-step auto-recall listeners then collide (see the README).
- insert:
    - id: hindsight
      name: dsh-plugin-hindsight-advanced
      disabled: true
      config:
        # REQUIRED — the only key with no default. Bank id (case-sensitive; the
        # server auto-creates it on first use). The bank is the OUTER isolation
        # boundary; inside it, memories live in three visibility tiers (see
        # retainScope below) that recall always sees together.
        bank: dsh

        # Hindsight REST base. Default: http://127.0.0.1:8888
        baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:9177

        # Optional; a CREDENTIAL REFERENCE, not the key — the value is
        # resolved per call through the credentials seam (process env,
        # ~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml, .env files), so the secret lives in the
        # 0600 store, never in this file. Add, e.g.:
        #   refs:
        #     HINDSIGHT_API_KEY: <the server's Bearer token>
        # to ~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml (or export it in the environment).
        apiKeyRef: HINDSIGHT_API_KEY

        # true — automatic recall on the first step of each turn. false — the
        # hindsight tool stays, the automatic recall goes.
        autoContext: true

        # true — the recall starts as the previous turn ends (in your think
        # time); from the second turn on it targets the previous message.
        # false — every turn queries the message you just sent and waits on
        # the server for it (up to autoContextTimeoutMs).
        prefetch: true

        # 5 — how many prior human turns ride along in the automatic
        # recall's query under a `Prior context:` block (one line per
        # user/assistant message; capped at 1000 chars, oldest lines drop
        # first). 1 — the single-message query the reference integrations
        # ship.
        recallContextTurns: 5

        # false - off. true - a LATER step of a running turn whose claim
        # carries no human message recalls, anchored on the previous step's
        # committed assistant message's visible TEXT blocks (the collapsed
        # row is labeled `recall:text - <ms>ms`); the step passes through
        # when the previous step has no text.
        # recallAfterText: false

        # false - off. true - the same mid-step recall, anchored on the
        # previous step's REASONING blocks instead (row label
        # `recall:think - <ms>ms`). Both keys on: a step carrying both
        # kinds gets ONE recall on one composed anchor (reasoning first,
        # then text; row label `recall:think+text - <ms>ms`), never two
        # lookups. A steering claim always wins the precedence.
        # recallAfterReasoning: false

        # false - off. true - the failure-lesson pass: a LATER step of a
        # running turn whose claim carries no human message matches the
        # previous step's committed TOOL CALLS against the bank'
        # experience-type memories (failure lessons); a match commits a
        # collapsed notice row (no label - just its summary) listing
        # up to actionLessonCandidates lessons, de-duplicated per turn by
        # memory id. A previous step without tool calls anchors nothing
        # (no bank call); subagent sessions stay silent.
        # actionLessons: false

        # The cap on how many lesson lines the notice row renders (the
        # recall is unbounded by this key; the row keeps the first N).
        # actionLessonCandidates: 10

        # false - off. true - right after a SUCCESSFUL context compaction
        # the bank is queried for the conversation's last human message
        # (the same composition as the prefetch: recallContextTurns
        # lines under `Prior context:`) and the snapshot lands on the
        # surface directly (row label `recall:compact - <ms>ms`): a
        # compaction fires outside any step (turn boundary, mid-step
        # under pressure, request retry), so there is no step to hang
        # the recall on. A failed compaction (an error) recalls nothing;
        # subagent sessions stay silent; the lookup is detached and
        # bounded by recallCompactTimeoutMs (its own bound - the composed
        # query is served slower than the single-message lookups, and the
        # shared autoContextTimeoutMs would time it out deterministically).
        # recallAfterCompaction: false

        # false - off. true - the pre-execution lesson gate: before a
        # call to a tool named in lessonGateTools is executed, the
        # PENDING call itself anchors a bounded recall on the bank's
        # experience-type memories (failure lessons); a hit whose match
        # score is at or above lessonGateMinScore DENIES the call
        # before the tool body runs - the rendered lessons travel as
        # the tool's error result, so the model learns from the recall
        # before the action acts. A sub-threshold hit, a timeout, an
        # aborted call, or a bank failure allows the call (no bank,
        # no gate); subagent sessions stay silent; the gate commits
        # nothing and is never de-duplicated (the denial is the
        # model's only feedback channel).
        # lessonGate: false

        # 0.3 - the minimum match score at which the gate denies a
        # gated call (a hit under the threshold, or a hit without any
        # score, allows the call).
        # lessonGateMinScore: 0.3

        # bash, run_code - the tool names the gate covers (only these
        # calls pay the pre-execution lookup; the default is the
        # side-effect-capable executors).
        # lessonGateTools: [bash, run_code]

        # true — the model surface is append-only: every committed recall
        # snapshot stays in the model context. false — the surface carries
        # only the LATEST full snapshot: each new one retires the
        # previously retained full card in place (a one-line tombstone
        # marker in the old slot, shadow-priced out of the metering) and
        # lands fresh at its own turn, while the durable log keeps every
        # full snapshot for replay and audit. Matches the llama-server
        # --no-reasoning-preserve naming: with it off, a turn's snapshot,
        # like its reasoning, lives for that turn only.
        recallPreserve: true

        # false — retain waits for the bank to process the memory, so the very
        # next recall already sees it. true — fast ack, background extraction.
        retainAsync: false

        # 4096 — token budget for recall responses.
        maxRecallTokens: 4096

        # 2500 — bound for the automatic lookup; a stopped/slow server never
        # blocks a turn.
        autoContextTimeoutMs: 2500

        # 8000 - bound for the DETACHED post-compaction lookup
        # (recallAfterCompaction). Its query is the full multi-turn
        # composition (anchor + `Prior context:` block), which the bank
        # serves slower than the single-message lookups, so it rides its
        # own bound; the event is fire-and-forget, so it never blocks a
        # turn.
        # recallCompactTimeoutMs: 8000

        # The visibility tier `retain` uses when the model omits the `scope`
        # parameter: 'global' (visible to every session of the bank),
        # 'preset' (this agent preset's sessions), or 'session' (this session
        # only). recall and reflect always see the session's own tier, its
        # preset's tier, and the global tier — never another session's or
        # preset's tier.
        retainScope: preset
        bankConfig:
          retain_mission: "Focus on the user's DSH workflow: durable decisions, project facts, and preferences worth recalling later. Ignore transient status and raw code."

readme.text: 🔴 Compatibility: this plugin tracks DeepSeek Harness commit 0d1f50007f9bca3f52b06e1c3074fa14d5fb0720 verbatim. It is NOT compatible with later DeepSeek Harness versions - they are too buggy to use.

A plugin for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) that integrates the Hindsight memory
system: your agent stores memories in your own Hindsight server and brings
the relevant ones back into the conversation.

With the `dsh` command:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/hindsight-advanced
```

When running dsh from source:

```bash
pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/hindsight-advanced
```

Then restart the server.

The configuration is one `hindsight` row in your own DSH config — never an
edit to the plugin's files. You place it in one of two spots - or both,
when the rows serve different banks (the profile-wide bank plus a
preset-specific bank; see Mounting the plugin twice below):

**Every session.** In your profile's patch layer
(`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`, append to your existing file):

```yaml
- id: hindsight
  disabled: false
  config:
    bank: my-bank

**One preset only.** In that preset's own file
(`~/.dsh/.agent-presets/<preset>/agent.cordis.yml`, append):

```yaml
- id: hindsight
  name: dsh-plugin-hindsight-advanced
  config:
    bank: my-bank

Presets that point at the same bank don't need separate banks — the
`preset` scope already keeps each preset's memories apart.

Two things to know about the row:

- the `config` block **replaces** the plugin's defaults wholesale — list
  every key you want; only `bank` is strictly required, the rest fall back
  to the defaults in the table below (but `baseUrl` and `apiKeyRef` are
  worth repeating, since their defaults point at port 8888 and carry no
  key);
- to switch the plugin off again, set `disabled: true` on the row (or
  remove the preset row) and restart.

Two rows can reach one session: the profile-wide row plus an agent-preset
row, against DIFFERENT banks. The session's PRESET mount then owns its
automatic recall: every automatic surface (the turn-start snapshot, the
mid-step recalls, the post-compaction recall, the lesson gate) commits ONE
snapshot - the preset bank's card - with the profile-wide bank's standing
directives merged in as their own section (headered by that bank), so the
profile-wide bank's rules keep reaching the model without a second block
per turn. The profile-wide row stays silent on every automatic surface for
that session: no second snapshot, no prefetch, no mid-step or
post-compaction recall, no gate lookup (its `hindsight` tool stays
registered, shadowed by the preset row's for that session's agents). A
session no preset row covers is served by the profile-wide row exactly as
usual. The merge is failure-isolated per bank: a profile-wide bank whose
directive listing fails is simply left out of the merge, the preset bank's
card still lands with its own rules. Mounting twice against the SAME bank
is redundant: the second mount's refreshes retire the first mount's cards,
so the surface converges on one bank's ca

| key | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bank` | — | **Required.** The name of the Hindsight bank to use (the server creates it on first use). |
| `baseUrl` | `http://127.0.0.1:8888` | Your Hindsight server's address. |
| `apiKeyRef` | — | **The way to give the plugin its key** — a *name* for the secret, not the secret itself. The value is looked up on every call (environment → `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` → `.env` files), so rotating the key needs no restart and the key never sits in a config file. See below. |
| `apiKey` | — | A plain key in the config, instead of a reference. Prefer `apiKeyRef`. |
| `autoContext` | `true` | Set `false` to turn off the automatic recall (each turn's first step, any human intervention claimed mid-turn, the mid-step agent-output recall, the post-compaction recall, and the opt-in pre-execution lesson gate; the `hindsight` tool stays). |
| `prefetch` | `true` | `true` (default): the recall starts as the *previous* turn ends, so from the second turn on it targets the previous message. `false`: every turn queries the message you just sent and waits on the server for it — the memory is always relevant to what you just said, at the cost of th

At the start of each turn the agent gets a small note: the memories that
match your latest message, plus any standing rules you stored. The lookup
starts in the background as soon as the *previous* turn ends — while you
are reading or typing — so by the time the agent starts the next turn the
memory is usually already there and the turn does not wait on the memory
server at all. The first turn of a conversation has nothing to read ahead
of, so it waits on the server normally (up to `autoContextTimeoutMs`).
Set `prefetch: false` to query the message you just sent instead — at the
cost of that wait on every turn.
If you send a message while the agent is already working, the recall
follows it: when the agent picks the intervention up at its next step it
recalls the bank on the spot (bounded by `autoContextTimeoutMs`),
anchored on the intervention itself, so a mid-turn correction arrives
with the memories about what it corrects. A step that only carries
plugin-injected context recalls nothing.
By default, that last sentence is the whole story: a step without a
human message recalls nothing. Set `recallAfterText: true` and/or
`recallAfterReasoning: true` to change it - at a step past th

`apiKeyRef: HINDSIGHT_API_KEY` is only a name — the plugin looks up the
value by that name on every call, in this order: the environment, then
`~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`, then `.env` files. The usual way is one line in
`~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`, **added alongside your existing entries**
(like the LLM key — don't replace them):

```yaml
version: 1
refs:
  HINDSIGHT_API_KEY: <the Hindsight server's token>
```
